messages:
Marta: FYI ticket #5541 from ACME. They report a continuous gap for audit events (service.auth.*) around 2026-03-03 03:00-04:30 UTC. SIEM shows no auth events. Can eng/security look? :eyes:
Vikram: On it. Any forwarder/exporter logs attached to the ticket? Missing auth events usually point to exporter auth failures, kms issues, or zero-byte manifests.
Dave: Pulled forwarder logs for tenant acme-prod in us-east-1 for that window. Key snippets below:
```
2026-03-03T03:02:11Z forwarder[acme-prod] WARN dispatch failed status=401 body="Unauthorized"
X-RateLimit-Limit: 100
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Retry-After: 34
```
and later:
```
2026-03-03T03:15:02Z forwarder[acme-prod] ERROR s3-upload failed Key=manifests/acme-prod/2026-03-03T03:14.manifest size=0
2026-03-03T03:16:01Z forwarder[acme-prod] ERROR kms.Decrypt DecryptionError: envelope key not found
```
Marta: Customer attached SIEM screenshot showing a straight hole for those auth events, asking if this is a retention setting or an internal outage.
Vikram: Looks like two correlated failures: (1) Downstream endpoint throttling caused 401/rate-limit retries; (2) KMS alias rotation happened around 03:10 and there were Decrypt failures after that. Together they produced blank manifests + decrypt errors.
Tom: ACME also ran a big deploy at ~03:00 which spiked export throughput. That likely amplified concurrency while rotation happened.
Vikram: Repro / triage steps for SRE/support:
1) Confirm retry / rate-limit patterns in forwarder logs for acme-prod. Example grep/jq snippet.
2) List manifests in S3 for the date range and check for size=0 files.
3) Query KMS/CloudTrail for Decrypt errors in the window.
4) Ensure forwarder role has kms:Decrypt on the new key ARN and that key policy includes the forwarder principal.
5) If zero-byte manifests found, schedule replay from raw event store.
Marta: I ran 1-3 already: found 5 zero-byte manifests between 03:10 and 03:18, and CloudTrail shows Decrypt failures from role/forwarder-acme-prod at 03:16:xx.
Vikram: Root cause hypothesis: transient downstream rate-limit -> heavy retry concurrency at forwarder + KMS alias rotation propagation delay causing decrypts to fail -> some manifests got uploaded as 0 bytes and some batches couldn't decrypt.
Dave: KMS rotation audit shows alias `alias/audit-forwarder-us` rotated at 2026-03-03T03:10:00Z; rotation completed but IAM propagation lag visible.
Tom: Customer confirmed they want us to replay; warned about potential duplicates. They've approved backfill.
Vikram: Immediate mitigations: (A) Ensure forwarder role has Decrypt on the new key ARN / update key policy if missing. (B) Replay the affected window after IAM fix. (C) Add a short-term concurrency/backoff based on X-RateLimit-* headers to avoid write races. Longer term: atomic manifest writes (write+rename), alerting on zero-byte manifests, and metric for decrypt-failure-rate.
Dave: I'll patch IAM if needed and run the replay. Planned command:
```
rb audit replay --tenant acme-prod --from 2026-03-03T03:00:00Z --to 2026-03-03T04:00:00Z --mode backfill --force
```
ETA ~40m after IAM change. Will post logs.
Marta: Notified ACME and got approval for replay. Asked for postmortem.
Vikram: For the postmortem include timeline, KMS alias rotation details, downstream rate-limit impact, and follow-ups: denylist zero-byte manifests from publishing, alert on >1 decrypt error/min, test alias swap procedure in staging, and add cooldown logic in forwarder.
audit-bot: incident created INC-2026-ACME-AUDIT-GAP assigned: eng-sre, eng-security.
Marta: Marking thread monitoring. Will update when replay completes. :thumbsup:
